title: Databricks Genie Review: Pricing, Limits and Alternatives
summary: Databricks Genie reviewed: how it works, how it is billed, where it stops, why it locks you in, and nao, the open source alternative.
body_markdown:
Databricks Genie answers questions on Databricks data, and only on Databricks data.


**Databricks Genie** is the natural-language chat built into Databricks: users ask questions about tables registered in Unity Catalog and get SQL, tables and charts back. Its usage is free until January 31, 2027 (compute is billed). It stops at the edge of Databricks: each Genie covers a capped set of tables, your data must be in Unity Catalog, your users need Databricks access, and your agent's context stays inside Databricks. **nao** is the open source alternative: an analytics agent your data team builds and controls, on any warehouse, Databricks included, with its context in files you own.


This review comes from our hands-on[benchmark of 20 analytics agents](https://getnao.io/blog/ai-data-agents-compared/) and from data teams we talked to who moved away from Genie.


## What is Databricks Genie?


Genie is now a family of products, and **Genie spaces are now called Genie Agents** :


- **Genie Agents** (formerly Genie spaces): a chat interface on a set of Unity Catalog tables, views and metric views, configured by a data author. This is what most people mean by "Databricks Genie".
- **Genie One** : a simpler interface for business users to discover and query data assets.
- **Genie Code** : the AI coding and data assistant for developers inside the workspace.


An author picks up to 50 tables, views or metric views, adds instructions and example SQL, and shares the agent. End users don't need warehouse permissions: the author's SQL warehouse runs the queries on their behalf. Genie reads Unity Catalog **metric views** (Databricks' semantic layer), and the Genie Agents API lets apps query an agent.


## How much does Databricks Genie cost?


Genie's billing has three parts (no amounts here: they change, check the[Genie pricing page](https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing/genie) ):


- **Genie Agents and Genie One usage is free for users through January 31, 2027.** Usage by service principals (for example an app calling the API) is billed.
- **Compute is billed separately** : the SQL warehouse (for example serverless SQL) that runs the queries.
- **Genie Code moved to pay-as-you-go on July 8, 2026** , with a free monthly allowance per user.


So the real question is not today's bill. It is what happens after the free period, how much warehouse compute your users generate, and whether you can leave if the price changes.


## Databricks Genie limitations


Teams look for a Databricks Genie alternative for five reasons we saw again and again:


1. **Many Genies, not one agent.** Each Genie Agent covers a limited set of tables (the docs cap it at 50 tables, views or metric views), configured for one domain. Companies end up with a sales Genie, a finance Genie, a product Genie, and users have to know which one to ask. A question that crosses domains has no single place to go. Data teams we talked to moved away from Genie for this reason.
2. **Limited context.** The agent knows what fits in its tables, instructions and example SQL. Your dbt docs, business rules and skills don't live there: dbt models only count once materialized in Unity Catalog, and we found no native dbt integration.
3. **Data must be in Unity Catalog.** Data in Postgres, BigQuery or Snowflake stays invisible.
4. **Users need Databricks access.** Users need a Databricks SQL or consumer entitlement plus SELECT on the data. Embedded agents prompt for a Databricks sign-in, and so does the Claude connector.
5. **Cost tied to Databricks.** Compute is always billed by Databricks, and user LLM usage is only free until January 2027.


## Should you build your analytics agent on Databricks Genie?


No, not if you want to keep control of it. An analytics agent is only as good as its context: the definitions, rules and examples your data team writes over months. Build it inside Genie and that context lives in Databricks' format, in Databricks' interface:


- **Vendor lock-in.** Your context is tied to Unity Catalog and Databricks metric views. Moving warehouses, or adding one, means rebuilding the agent from scratch.
- **Your costs follow Databricks pricing.** Compute, models and the end of the free period are decided by your warehouse vendor, not by you.
- **Your agent's ceiling is Databricks' roadmap.** If Genie doesn't read your dbt project or support a new kind of context, you wait.


Keep the warehouse and the agent separate. With nao, the context is plain files in your own git repo: readable, versioned, reviewed like code, and portable. Switching or adding a warehouse is a config change, not a rebuild.


## nao: the open source alternative to Databricks Genie


**nao is open source (Apache 2.0).** You can read every line of the agent, self-host it on your own infrastructure or run it on nao Cloud, and bring the LLM of your choice. You don't pay before you see value.


Databricks Genie nao


License Proprietary, part of Databricks **Open source, Apache 2.0**


Where it runs In your Databricks workspace Self-hosted or nao Cloud


Warehouses Databricks only Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, Postgres, Redshift, DuckDB and more


Agent scope One Genie per set of up to 50 tables One agent over your whole context


Context Tables, instructions, example SQL, metric views Files in your repo: schemas, previews, profiling, dbt docs,` RULES.md` , semantic layer, skills


Evaluation Built in` nao test` on your own questions


Who can ask Users with Databricks access Anyone you invite, in nao Chat, Slack, Teams or Claude


LLM Run by Databricks Yours: Claude, GPT, Gemini, Mistral, Ollama...


### How to build an analytics agent on Databricks with nao


Keep Databricks as your warehouse and run nao on top. The setup is five steps:


1. ` pip install nao-core` , then` nao init` and pick Databricks as the warehouse.
2. ` nao sync` writes your Databricks metadata (columns, previews, profiling) as files, next to your dbt project and docs.
3. Write the business rules in` RULES.md` : which table is the source of truth, how dates work, what each metric means. Our[context engineering guide](https://getnao.io/blog/how-to-do-context-engineering-for-data-teams/) covers the method.
4. Write 20-40 real questions with their answers and run[nao test](https://getnao.io/blog/analytics-agent-benchmark-context-stack/) after every change.
5. Deploy nao Chat for your users, or plug it into[Slack](https://getnao.io/blog/setup-ai-analytics-slack-bot-open-source/) , Teams or Claude through the[nao MCP](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-mcp/) . They don't need Databricks accounts.


That is how our own agent went[from 45% to 86% reliability](https://getnao.io/blog/improve-analytics-agent-reliability-steps/) . The same context works the day you add a second warehouse.
